prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An optical device for the stabilization of images, including a first deformable membrane and a second deformable membranes, a support to which a respective peripheral anchoring area of each of said membranes is connected, and a constant volume of fluid enclosed between the first and the second membrane, said fluid producing mechanical coupling of said first and second membranes. The optical device also includes: a first actuation device of a region of the first membrane located between the peripheral anchoring area and a central part of the first membrane; and a second actuation device of a region of the second membrane located between the peripheral anchoring area and a central part of the second membrane. A control means of the first and second actuation devices is configured, from a rest position where the first and second actuation devices are inactive, to have multiple operating modes to apply respective actuation voltage to the first actuation device or the second actuation device.

The optical image-stabilization device comprises first and second deformable membranes, each connected to a support along a peripheral anchoring area. The two membranes define an enclosed space containing a substantially constant volume of fluid. This fluid mechanically couples the membranes so that deformation of one membrane produces a corresponding response in the other.

A first actuation device is configured to control a region of the first membrane located between its peripheral anchoring area and its central part. Similarly, a second actuation device controls a corresponding region of the second membrane between its peripheral anchoring area and central part.

A control system selectively applies an actuation voltage to either the first or the second actuation device, starting from an inactive rest position. By independently or selectively driving the actuators, the control system provides multiple operating modes for deforming the membranes and thereby performing optical image stabilization.
outputs.L4:
An optical image-stabilization device includes first and second deformable optical membranes arranged opposite one another. Each membrane is secured around its peripheral region to a supporting structure, while an intermediate region remains movable. The space between the membranes contains a substantially incompressible fluid and forms a sealed, substantially constant-volume chamber. As a result, displacement of one membrane changes the pressure or fluid distribution within the chamber and produces a corresponding displacement of the other membrane.

A first actuator is mechanically coupled to the intermediate region of the first membrane, and a second actuator is mechanically coupled to the intermediate region of the second membrane. The actuators may deform the membranes by moving, tilting, bending, or otherwise displacing their intermediate regions relative to the anchored peripheral regions. Because the membranes are coupled through the constant-volume fluid, actuation of either membrane influences the position and curvature of both membranes. This arrangement permits the optical surfaces to be adjusted in a coordinated manner while maintaining the volume of the enclosed fluid.

A controller is electrically connected to the first and second actuators and supplies selectable drive voltages to one or both actuators. The controller may operate the device in multiple modes. In a first mode, the controller drives the first actuator while the second actuator remains unpowered or is held at a reference voltage. In a second mode, the controller drives the second actuator while the first actuator remains unpowered or is held at a reference voltage. In additional modes, both actuators may be driven simultaneously, sequentially, or with different voltage amplitudes, polarities, phases, or timing relationships.

By selecting the actuator and the applied voltage, the controller can produce different combinations of membrane displacement, curvature, and angular orientation. Sensor signals representing camera motion, optical-axis deviation, or image displacement may be used to determine the required drive voltages. The controller can then deform the fluid-coupled membranes to redirect or modify the incident light path and compensate for unwanted motion. The availability of multiple operating modes allows the device to adapt its stabilization response to changing motion conditions, optical requirements, power constraints, or actuator characteristics, thereby providing controllable and versatile optical image stabilization.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an optical image-stabilization device using two fluid-coupled deformable membranes and independently controlled actuators.
counterfactuals.output: An optical image-stabilization device includes a fluid-filled chamber having first and second optically transmissive deformable membranes disposed along an optical path and fluidly coupled through the chamber. First and second actuator assemblies are respectively coupled to the first and second membranes and are independently controllable to vary membrane shape, position, or orientation. A controller receives motion information from one or more sensors and drives the actuator assemblies to produce coordinated deformations of the membranes, thereby generating a controllable angular deflection, lateral displacement, and/or optical-power adjustment of light passing through the chamber. Fluid displaced by deformation of one membrane may be redistributed toward the other membrane, enabling complementary or differential deformation while maintaining a substantially sealed fluid volume. Independent actuation permits correction of image motion about multiple axes and compensation for optical aberrations or focus variation. The device may be incorporated into a camera, imaging module, or other optical system to stabilize an image without translating a lens assembly or image sensor.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an optical device that stabilizes images through first and second deformable membranes enclosing a constant volume of fluid, including its actuation and control mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output:
The device is a fluid-filled adaptive optical element positioned in an imaging light path. It includes:

- **First and second transparent deformable membranes** mounted opposite one another on a rigid frame.
- A sealed chamber between the membranes containing a substantially incompressible, optically transparent fluid of **constant volume**.
- One or more **actuators** coupled to peripheral or selected regions of each membrane. The actuators—such as piezoelectric, electromagnetic, electrostatic, or shape-memory elements—apply differential forces that bend or tilt the membranes. Because the fluid volume is fixed, inward displacement of one membrane produces a corresponding outward displacement of the other.

By applying unequal actuation around the membrane peripheries, the device forms a controllable wedge or prism that changes the propagation direction of light, thereby shifting the image on an image sensor. Symmetric actuation may also vary optical power or correct focus and aberrations.

A controller receives motion information from gyroscopes, accelerometers, or image-based motion estimation. It calculates the optical deflection needed to oppose camera movement and drives the actuators through suitable voltage or current amplifiers. Position, pressure, or membrane-shape sensors may provide closed-loop feedback so that the commanded membrane profiles are accurately maintained. The controller continuously updates the actuator signals, causing the adaptive element to steer the incoming image in the opposite direction to detected vibration and thus stabilize the image without changing the enclosed fluid volume.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of a membrane-based optical image stabilizer with peripheral anchoring, mechanical coupling by fluid, and multiple voltage-controlled operating modes.
counterfactuals.output: A membrane-based optical image stabilizer uses a transparent, deformable membrane fixed around its periphery to define a fluid-filled optical chamber. Motion of an actuator or opposing membrane is transmitted through the substantially incompressible fluid, mechanically coupling separated regions without rigid linkages. Independently addressable electrodes apply controlled voltages to electrostatically deform or tilt the membrane, changing the optical surface and redirecting the image. Different voltage patterns provide multiple operating modes, including tip/tilt stabilization, focus or optical-power adjustment, higher-order aberration correction, and a neutral or locked state. Peripheral anchoring maintains sealing and positional stability while allowing the central optical aperture to deform.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the construction and operation of a dual-membrane optical stabilization device in formal patent language, specifying the support, anchoring regions, enclosed fluid, actuators, rest position, and operating modes.
counterfactuals.output:
An optical stabilization device may comprise a support defining an optical aperture and carrying first and second optically transmissive, elastically deformable membranes. The first membrane may be secured to the support along a first anchoring region, and the second membrane may be secured to the support along a second anchoring region spaced from and arranged opposite the first anchoring region. The membranes and an intervening portion of the support collectively delimit a sealed cavity containing an optically transmissive fluid. The fluid preferably substantially fills the cavity and is selected to transmit pressure between the membranes while permitting controlled variation of the optical geometry of the device.

One or more actuators may be mechanically coupled to respective actuation regions of the first membrane, the second membrane, or both membranes. Each actuation region may be disposed radially inward of, radially outward of, or otherwise spaced from the corresponding anchoring region. The actuators may comprise piezoelectric, electrostatic, electromagnetic, thermal, pneumatic, hydraulic, or shape-memory actuators and may be independently or jointly controlled by a controller responsive to an optical-stabilization signal.

In a rest position, corresponding to an unenergized or predetermined bias condition of the actuators, the membranes assume respective nominal shapes and the fluid occupies a nominal cavity volume. The nominal shapes may be planar, substantially planar, curved, or mutually complementary. The rest position establishes a nominal optical axis and a nominal optical power, which may be zero or nonzero.

During operation, displacement of an actuation region deforms at least one membrane and produces a redistribution or pressure change of the enclosed fluid. Because the fluid is confined within the sealed cavity, deformation of one membrane may induce a corresponding deformation of the other membrane. Selective control of the actuators thereby changes the inclination, curvature, axial position, or a combination thereof, of the fluid-bounded optical surfaces.

In a stabilization mode, the actuators may be operated differentially to produce an asymmetric or wedge-shaped deformation of the membranes, thereby deflecting transmitted light and compensating for angular or lateral motion of an associated imaging system. In an optical-power mode, the actuators may be operated symmetrically or in common mode to vary the curvature of one or both membranes and thereby adjust focus or optical power. In a combined mode, common-mode and differential actuation components may be superimposed to provide simultaneous focus adjustment and image stabilization. In a neutral or hold mode, the actuators may maintain the membranes at the rest position or at a selected biased position. The controller may switch among said modes and regulate the actuators in open-loop or closed-loop operation using signals from one or more motion, position, pressure, wavefront, or image sensors.
